sealed_before: any analysis load of fund prices
windows_authority: config/windows.json (unchanged); half A = daily rows dated strictly before 2013-01-01

data.load_guard: filter date < 2013-01-01 at read AND assert max loaded date < 2013-01-01 after load; assert each ticker's raw span extends to or past 2013-01-01 so the half-A slice is not a truncation

interpretation_rulings.question: The brief lists 'cash: SHY' inside the asset-class list. Is SHY a sixth weighted class?
interpretation_rulings.ruling: NO. SHY is the cash proxy and the risk-free leg, not a weighted sleeve. Five weighted classes over sixteen ETFs.
grounds: Section A names the sixteen ETFs and then 'plus SHY (the cash proxy)'.
The TREND rule's fallback is 'otherwise it holds SHY', which makes a SHY sleeve self-referential and vacuous.
'BUY-AND-HOLD book: the same weights, always holding the ETF' would put a permanent 1/6 in cash, contradicting the sprint's 'buy-and-hold of the same ETFs'.
'time in cash by class' would read a constant 100% for a cash class.
interpretation_rulings.mitigation: The six-class variant dSR is additionally reported as a descriptive robustness line so the ruling is falsifiable from the artifact.

interpretation_rulings.ruling: Traded notional is measured on weights aggregated by ASSET, not by sleeve: two sleeves sitting in SHY are one SHY position.
interpretation_rulings.grounds: That is the notional actually traded; per-sleeve accounting would charge offsetting trades that never reach the market.

interpretation_rulings.ruling: Weights drift with realised returns inside the month; turnover is measured between the drifted weights and the next month's target weights. Cost is charged to the month the new positions earn.
interpretation_rulings.note: Cost is not compounded into the drift (second order).

interpretation_rulings.ruling: 'worst 12 months' = the worst rolling twelve-month NET total return.

States are decided at month-end t and earn in month t+1. The first scored month is the first RETURN month, i.e. the month after the first month-end with at least two classes eligible. Both months are stated.

universe.monthly_price: the last closeadj of each calendar month
universe.eligibility: a sleeve is eligible from the first month-end at which it has 10 month-end closes
universe.class_weight: 1 / (number of classes with at least one eligible member), recomputed each month-end
universe.within_class_weight: equal across that class's eligible members

books.TREND: each sleeve holds its ETF for the following month when its month-end closeadj is above the mean of its last 10 month-end closeadj (current month included); otherwise it holds SHY
books.BUY_AND_HOLD: the same weights, always holding the ETF

costs.applied_to: both books, on traded notional (switches and rebalancing)

statistic.sharpe: annualised Sharpe of monthly returns in EXCESS of SHY: mean/std * sqrt(12), std ddof=1
statistic.dSR: annualised Sharpe of TREND NET minus annualised Sharpe of BUY-AND-HOLD NET, over the same months

voting_null.name: random-timing books (two-state Markov at the book-under-test's own measured rates)
voting_null.rates: per sleeve, p01 and p10 estimated from the state path of the book under test over consecutive eligible month pairs; initial state drawn from the implied stationary distribution
voting_null.degenerate_rates: n0 == 0 -> p01 = 1.0; n1 == 0 -> p10 = 0.0; p01 + p10 == 0 -> stationary set to the empirical mean state
voting_null.p: the share of random books with dSR >= the dSR of the book under test
voting_null.what_it_asks: whether the rule times better than chance AT THE SAME CASH LEVEL AND TURNOVER
voting_null.what_the_rate_measurement_leaks: measuring the switching reveals FREQUENCY, not PERFORMANCE: the rates fix how often a random book switches and hence its invested share, never when the switches fall
voting_null.why_not_a_no_information_null_against_bu: random timing at invested share k carries a Sharpe near sqrt(k) of buy-and-hold, so a no-information null sits BELOW zero and a positive dSR against it would be unearned
voting_null.uniformity: the same procedure is applied to every book under test: its own rates are measured, a fresh null is generated at those rates, p is read off

order_of_operations: 1. MDE: the dSR detectable at 80% power from the random books' spread
2. KNOWN-NULL CONTROL: 200 random-timing books fed in as the observed book, each against a fresh 500-book null; the share at p <= 0.05 must lie in [0.01, 0.10] or HALT

3. POSITIVE CONTROL: semi-synthetic on the real half-A ETF data; each sleeve's state set to the sign of its next-month excess return with probability q and the opposite otherwise; q calibrated on ONE draw so dSR is about 0.4; then 50 fresh draws, detection at p <= 0.05 must be >= 0.80 or HALT

controls.mde_definition: (null p95 - null median) + z(0.80) * sd(null dSR), z(0.80) = 0.8416

positive_control.leak: DELIBERATE and named by a test: the planted state reads the sign of the return it is about to earn

observed_emissions: per book: CAGR, annual vol, Sharpe, maximum drawdown, worst rolling 12 months
paired stationary-block bootstrap (mean block 6, R = 5000, ONE shared month index, seed 20261005) 90% interval for dSR and for the mean monthly return difference - REPORTED, NOT VOTING
time in cash by class; switches per year
dSR with calendar 2008 excluded - DESCRIPTIVE, measuring how much the result rests on one event
STRESS dSR at 15 bps per side

verdict.SOMETHING: timing p <= 0.05 AND dSR > 0 -> promoted to one registered half-B look (2013-2020)
verdict.SUGGESTIVE: p in (0.05, 0.10] with dSR > 0 -> recorded, not promoted

prior_stated_now: SOMETHING. Half A holds 2001-2002 and 2008, the declines trend timing is known for side-stepping; the decisive question is half B, where the literature reports timing roughly matching or trailing buy-and-hold. A SOMETHING here is expected and settles little on its own.

dating_test.purpose: establish whether the vendor's daily valuation table is as-filed (point-in-time usable) or restated
dating_test.units_resolved_from_dictionary: marketcap is USD MILLIONS; netinccmnusd is USD; implied earnings are therefore scaled by 1e6 before comparison
dating_test.dictionary_note: for AR dimensions (ART) the fundamentals date IS the SEC filing date; for MR dimensions (MRT) it is the reportperiod - this is what makes the contrast readable
dating_test.statistic: implied trailing earnings E(t) = marketcap / pe each day; locate the days E steps; compare each step date with the ART filing dates and reportperiods
dating_test.classification: a step on or after a filing date is AS-FILED (point-in-time usable); a step before its filing date is LOOK-AHEAD
dating_test.caveat: assumes the free sample is built the same way as the paid table
dating_test.brief_discrepancy_recorded: the brief states KO, NKE and WMT were all answered on the free tier in R3-0; the R3-0 manifest contains no KO, NKE or WMT request (its ten metrics names were AAPL MSFT JPM XOM JNJ MVL SMTL NRGN MAXX TRAC, and the daily and fundamentals per-ticker gate probes were issued for TSLA and answered 403 'Exceeds free tier'). The premise is therefore UNVERIFIED at sealing and is settled empirically by the requests themselves.
